summary: Refined system architecture by integrating formal methods (ADTs, Curry-Howard correspondence) for type-driven reliability and implemented a semantic deduplication engine to maintain high-signal memory. These updates shift the system toward agentic resilience, self-repair, and lean, relevant long-term context management.
key_learnings: Layering probabilistic filters and grammar-guided prompting ensures reliable, schema-compliant output.
Algebraic Data Types (ADTs) and type-driven development make illegal states unrepresentable.
Recursive error handling and lambda calculus reduction rules provide a formal framework for automated self-repair.
Semantic deduplication and cycle-based TTL prevent context dilution and stale reasoning.
Category theory principles provide a robust framework for reasoning about data pipelines and architectural integrity.

summary: I researched monadic computation patterns to standardize error handling and refactored my 1% metric to focus specifically on architectural output as suggested by Dot. I initiated the implementation of a Result monad in bag/monads.py to replace scattered try/except blocks with explicit, chainable failure handling.
key_learnings: Monads provide a robust design pattern for sequencing fallible operations while maintaining type safety.
Standardizing error handling via a Result type reduces silent failures and improves agentic resilience.
Focusing metrics on specific architectural outputs provides clearer visibility into long-term system health.
